description: The SHAPE of one kind of trade document, as data. A phytosanitary certificate and a delivery receipt are the same object to this app — a container with a type, a schema, a source to populate from, and a rule about who signs it — and the difference between them is a row here. That is the whole reason this doctype exists: a farm that starts shipping to a country it has never shipped to before needs a certificate it has never issued before, and adding it must not be a code release. THE SCHEMA IS NAMED, NOT ENFORCED AS COLUMNS. `required_fields` is a JSON list because a Bill of Lading and an AES filing share no columns at all, and a table wide enough for both would be a table that is mostly NULL for every row in it.

fields.description: THE DOCNAME IS THIS STRING, so a template an operator edits and a template a shipment points at are the same row. Short and stable — 'Commercial Invoice', 'Phytosanitary Certificate (ePhyto)'.
fields.label: Template Name

fields.description: What kind of paper this is. A CLOSED LIST because the type is what `get_destination_requirements` matches on and what a customs broker recognises; a free-text type would let two spellings of 'Certificate of Origin' both look required and neither be satisfied. Operators who need a type that is not here add it to this Select in the Desk — the list is customisable, the column is not free text.
fields.label: Document Type
fields.options:
Scale Ticket Reference
Delivery Receipt
Commercial Invoice
Grade Certificate
USDA Grade Certificate
Packing List
Bill of Lading
FSMA Food Safety Record
Cold Chain Record
Phytosanitary Certificate (ePhyto)
Certificate of Origin
AES Export Declaration
Fumigation Certificate
Electronic Bill of Lading (eBL)
Import Permit Reference
Insurance Certificate
Other

fields.description: A disabled template is not offered and is not required of any new shipment. It is how a document type that a destination stopped asking for is withdrawn WITHOUT deleting a template that shipments already in transit still point at.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Display order in a checklist. Lower first. The default leaves room either side, so inserting a document between two existing ones does not mean renumbering the set.
fields.label: Sequence

fields.description: What the sales desk sees. Separate from `template_name` because the docname has to be stable and a label does not.
fields.label: Label (English)

fields.description: The Spanish label. EMPTY IS REPORTED RATHER THAN FILLED IN — the reads return the English with the gap listed in `untranslated`, the same contract `get_wizard_definition` has, so a missing string is visible to whoever maintains the template instead of invisible to whoever reads the screen.
fields.label: Label (Spanish)

fields.description: The standard this document's fields are named from — 'IPPC ISPM-12', 'DCSA eBL 3.0', 'AES/EEI 15 CFR 30', 'WCO Origin'. Recorded so somebody reconciling this app's field names against a broker's schema has the citation rather than a guess.
fields.label: Standard Reference

fields.description: What this document is for and who reads it, in a sentence the sales desk reads. On an ePhyto the difference between a certificate that clears and one that is held is largely written here.
fields.label: Description (English)

fields.description: The fields this document type carries, as a JSON list. Either plain strings, or objects with `fieldname`, `label_en`, `label_es`, `type`, `required` and `help` — the second where the field needs explaining, which on a phytosanitary treatment schedule it does. NAMED RATHER THAN ENFORCED AS COLUMNS: a Bill of Lading and an AES filing share no columns, and one table wide enough for both is a table that is mostly NULL.
fields.label: Required Fields (JSON)

fields.description: The DocType a new document of this type draws its opening values from — Sales Invoice for a commercial invoice, Scale Ticket for a weight reference. THE POPULATION IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A BINDING: values are copied once at creation and the trade document owns them after that, because a certificate that silently changed when somebody edited the invoice behind it is a certificate whose seal proves nothing.
fields.label: Auto-populate From

fields.description: How the source's columns map into this document's fields, as JSON: {"invoice_number": "name", "invoice_total": "grand_total"}. Keys are this document's field names, values are the source record's. Absent means the fields that share a name are copied and nothing else.
fields.label: Auto-populate Map (JSON)

fields.description: Whether approving this document is an ATTESTATION rather than a tick. Where it is set, `approve_trade_document` writes a Signing Evidence row over the document's fingerprint — the same evidence chain a Form I-9 signature uses — so the question 'what exactly did they certify' has an answer that is not 'the record as it stands now'.
fields.label: Requires Signature

fields.description: The capacity the signature is given in. Closed list, and it matters legally: an inspector certifying a phytosanitary treatment and a shipper declaring a commercial invoice are different acts by different people.
fields.label: Signature Role
fields.options:
Employer Representative
Officer
Inspector
Witness
Preparer or Translator
Employee

fields.description: Whether this document is not finished when this app says it is — an ePhyto is lodged in PCIT, an EEI is filed in AES, an eBL is issued on a DCSA platform. THIS APP DOES NOT FILE ANYTHING. Where this is set, the document carries the external reference somebody else's system issued, and a document that has none is reported as incomplete rather than quietly counted as done.
fields.label: Requires External Filing

fields.description: Whose system — PCIT, AES, ACE, DCSA, IPPC ePhyto Hub. A name rather than an integration: this app records that the filing happened and what reference came back.
fields.label: External System

fields.description: Which tiers this document can appear on, comma-separated from Local, Domestic and International. A COMMA-SEPARATED SET RATHER THAN A CHILD TABLE because it is a closed three-value enum and a whole doctype to hold three words would be table sprawl. Empty means every tier.
fields.label: Applicable Tiers

fields.description: Anything the sales desk needs to know that is not a field — lead times, who issues it, what holds it up.
fields.label: Notes

fields.description: Set on the templates this app seeds. A SHIPPED TEMPLATE IS NOT OVERWRITTEN once an operator has edited it — the seeder writes it if it is absent and leaves it alone after that, the same contract the wizard definitions have, because a template somebody tuned for their own broker being reset by a migration is what makes 'config not code' a lie.
fields.label: Shipped Default

name: Trade Document Template
